messages:
harlan: heads up — I’m seeing a wave of small-pod evictions in us-west1c over the past ~45m. warm-pools show 18% more pending tiny pods and a few latebind collisions. cc @kai @neha
infra-bot: ALERT scheduler.evictions.high us-west1c 2023-11-02T14:30Z — evict_rate: 22/min :warning:
kai: yup, the scheduler traces show repeated lease handshake timeouts during allocation. lots of tiny-gang churn, latebind windows aligning and causing back-and-forth scheduling
neha: quick dump from one affected node: `kubectl get pods -o wide --field-selector spec.nodeName=node-22` shows many pending tiny pods with affinity=spread and taints not tolerated. also seeing: `lease_failures=37; nvlink_errors=12`
olga: noticed nvlink latency spikes on rack-22 last night (packet drops -> handshake retries). that will amplify latebind collisions and cause the descheduler to thrash :thinking_face:
ben: cost side — fallback to larger instance shapes when small racks fail is pushing burst spend ~12% this window. we should be careful with any temporary fallback policies
harlan: proposal: 1) run a short descheduler job to coalesce tiny pods onto healthy racks 2) temporarily widen latebind window from 30s -> 60s to reduce collision rate 3) add a canary to avoid mass churn. Command I plan to run: ```kubectl apply -f descheduler-job-usw1c.yaml```
kai: agree on descheduler. also think we should sweep for stale taints like `gpu:reserved=yes:NoSchedule` that are stuck on a subset of nodes. I can send a canary patch to mark tolerations on a small subset
neha: attaching quick diag excerpt (copied): `scheduler.trace: node=node-22 lease_timeout=120s err=handshake_failed; nvlink_err=4` — will collect full traces and drop in the incident thread
olga: oncall/eng-sre — if evictions exceed 30/min I’ll escalate. running `ss -s` and `nvidia-smi topo --matrix` now to confirm inter-node fabric health
infra-bot: DESCHEDULER job started by kai at 2023-11-02T15:02Z — job_id=ds-8342
ben: flag — autoscaler is still aggressively provisioning new warm nodes in that AZ. can we increase cooldown to avoid immediate fallback allocations while we stabilize? that reduces cost churn
harlan: will draft runbook: "run descheduler -> widen latebind -> monitor 15m -> adjust autoscaler cooldown -> if no improvement rollback". I’ll post the runbook in the incident channel and attach metrics
kai: PR created for canary tolerations: #3421. canary targets rack-21 only for 1h
neha: collecting eviction logs + pod yamls; will paste snippets into p0 channel and link the traces
olga: :thumbsup: keep me posted, I’ll keep monitoring nvlink metrics and report any infra-level flakiness
ben: also logging a cost impact note for finance so they aren’t surprised if AWS spend spikes for the hour
harlan: thanks team — running descheduler now and will watch evict rate. ping here with any new anomalies
